messages:
Hannah: Quick thread: we need clearer rules for capability gating + rate-hedging when routing between hosted/dedicated/private. Too many silent fallbacks causing surprise latency/cost spikes.
Jorge: Agreed. My proposal: make three orthogonal pieces explicit in the handshake + routing decision: capability set, hedging policy (none/egress/duplicate), and cost-latency hint (favor_latency/favor_cost).
Mei: Love the separation. Can we have tiny example of how route config would look?
Jorge: Sure, simple example: 
```yaml
route: /v1/generate
requires: [kv_cache, streaming]
hedging: duplicate_if_no_response_ms: 250
hint: favor_latency
```
Mei: That makes it actionable. Who enforces the "requires" semantics? Controller or gateway?
Alex: Gateway should consult a capability registry cached in the control-plane. At attach time, nodes publish a capability manifest. If a requirement isn't met, we consult the route's fallback table to pick an alternative model or return a deterministic rejection.
Hannah: Important: distinguish soft vs hard requirements. E.g., streaming is soft if we can provide chunked polling fallback; hsm is hard if customer policy forbids software KMS.
Jorge: Implementation sketch: node registers as {capabilities: [...], modes: [candidate|active|drain], metadata: {latency_p50: 12ms}}. Controller treats candidate as non-routable for hard requirements.
Mei: We must surface which fallback was used in API responses and metrics. Example trace tag: routing.fallback=model_quantized.v2 or routing.reject_reason=hsm_missing.
Alex: On hedging: duplicate hedges to hosted only if the request is idempotent or safe to dedupe; otherwise use egress hedging (start second attempt on different capacity class) or increase timeout. We need a hedging policy DSL small enough to review.
Hannah: Edge case: Dedicated pools might advertise higher throughput but worse p99 because of multi-tenancy. Our selector should consider p50/p95/p99 distributions in manifest, not only binary capability flags.
Jorge: Good call. Manifest example with perf buckets: 
```json
{ "capabilities": ["kv_cache"], "perf": {"p50_ms":"10","p95_ms":"60","p99_ms":"200"} }
```
Mei: For upgrades: when a node flips from candidate->active for a new capability, delay routing by warmup windows (observed-successful-requests >= N and no errors for M minutes). Also don't enable hedging to the new capability for first K minutes.
Alex: Testing plan: unit tests for manifest parsing, integration test with simulated private sidecar lacking HSM + route with hard_hsm requirement -> expect 403 + metric routing.reject.hsm. End-to-end with chaos: randomly drop backend and validate hedging doesn't double-charge billing.
Hannah: Migration checklist for Dedicated -> Private: backfill manifests, reconcile perf tags, set default route hints to favor_cost for initial 2 weeks, monitor routing.fallback rate and p99. If fallback > 2% alert SRE.
Jorge: Ops note: add route-level override to force "strict" mode (fail early if any hard requirement missing) for customers who need determinism. Default remains permissive with documented fallbacks.
Mei: UX: console should show "capability heatmap" and highlight routes using fallbacks. Devs should be able to test their route against a "capability matrix" simulator.
Alex: I'll sketch a brief RFC: schema, handshake states, hedging DSL, perf bucketing, and migration steps. Will include small API change: /internal/v1/node/capabilities -> returns JSON manifest.
deploy-bot: infra: canary tool available at infra/canaries/hedge-gate. Run `/deploy canary hedge-gate` to exercise hedging behavior.
Hannah: Assign reviewers: Jorge + Mei. Add a checklist item: ensure billing idempotency for duplicate hedged requests.
Jorge: I'll add a short appendix on billing safety and de-dup tokens.
Mei: Great. If RFC is ready by Friday we can run a canary next week.
Hannah: Thanks all. Small RFC please, focused examples. :rocket:
